screens.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup, precise-object-edit.
EDIT the provided full desktop interface image into a new coherent design version. Keep the same complete screen, monochrome white-and-black fixed-width native patch typography, product "unit~", project "morning-study", selected separate page, and the existing functional source separation workflow. Keep one 24-second input morning-study.wav at 44.1 kHz and FOUR independent outputs vocals~, drums~, bass~, other~, each covering the same 0:00–0:24. Keep meaningful detailed black waveform content, import/export, solo/mute, global play/stop/loop and preview source/stem. This is a visual shape-language refinement, not a different app or feature.

PRIMARY CHANGE: remove the rigid rectangular-box look throughout the interface. Introduce a restrained mixed geometry based on patch graphics, open contours and precise inline controls. DO NOT merely replace every rectangle with a rounded rectangle.

Top identity: the small u~ symbol and unit~ text remain, but the logo can use tiny cropped-corner strokes rather than a heavy enclosing square. Header/file-edit-view remain compact. The navigation "separate", "transcribe", "compose" are plain short monospace text, with an underline beneath separate instead of a row of boxed buttons. Left Notes / Rhythm / Chords / Audio navigation is plain text; Audio selected by a short underline or a small dot, no closed rectangle.

The input~ module at top center and the four waveform outputs MUST NOT be closed thick rectangular cards. Instead, each musical object is a readable open group: module name with a short thin heading divider, small exposed circle inlet/outlet, corner marks or short cropped/chamfered contour fragments, and a waveform with only a fine baseline/time ticks and soft curved trim-end brackets. Some tiny open corner marks may have slight curvature, some cropped chamfers, but leave the long module boundaries open. No full 4-sided boxes around the waveforms. Keep compact spacing and a clear two-column / two-row output arrangement.

Core "separate~" is the one compact processing operator: a distinctive short elongated operator body with chamfered left shoulder and a softly arced right end, or a subtle compact curved-end polygon. This operator may have a complete thin outline unlike the open audio groups. Include "4 stems", a small oval run action, unboxed cancel text, and "complete 100%" with a thin simple progress line. One small CIRCULAR input port at top connects from input~. EXACTLY FOUR small CIRCULAR output ports along lower edge each feed one and only one output waveform group via four thin smooth black curved patch cords. Draw each wire independently from separate~ to its destination: vocals~, drums~, bass~, other~. Use clear fan-out routing with room between curves. The lower-output cords may route outside the upper groups. There must be NO wire from vocals~ to bass~, no wire from drums~ to other~, no stem-to-stem connection, no shared junction after the four separate~ output ports, and no port touching the wrong group. This is parallel source separation, never a serial chain. Exposed wave-group inlet circles sit beside each group title to keep cord logic readable.

Solo/mute under each output use small circular or diamond toggles with short monospace text, not square framed boxes. Export.wav uses simple borderless text with a small arrow, or an understated oval outline, never another rectangle. Preview: source / stem is a compact textual pair with an underline under stem, no surrounding rectangle.

Right Inspector: remove its large outer closed border entirely. Keep "selection: vocals~", thin short dividers and all useful fields. Numerical controls gain 0.0 dB, start 0.00, end 24.00 are INLINE UNDERLINED numbers, with no boxed inputs. The vertical gain control is a thin line slider with small circular handle, not a thick rectangular fader. Mono / mute / audio on use little circles or diamonds, selected audio on marked by a small black center. Change misleading metadata from "file: morning-study.wav" to "source: morning-study.wav", retaining format 44.1 kHz, length 00:24.0, channels 2 (stereo).

Bottom transport tools are small circle play/stop symbols or compact oval/borderless labels. 112 BPM, 4/4, stereo are plain inline labels with understated underline when editable, no repeated rectangular controls. Bottom volume is a fine line with a small round handle, -6.0 dB label.

Aim for a thoughtful black-and-white instrument-like utility interface with different clear shapes for source, processing, results and controls. Fine 1px lines, open corner marks, circles, diamonds and cropped ends. Crisp small fixed-width typography and compact native-tool density. Preserve readable exact functional labels. The page should remain a full usable desktop software screenshot, no perspective, no device border or wallpaper.

Avoid big rounded dashboard cards, uniformly rounded rectangles, closed heavy boxes, decorative shapes, colors, gray fills except very light selection if needed, gradients, glows, shadows, 3D, AI assistant/chat/magic effects, marketing slogans, changed durations, missing stems, stem-to-stem serial patching. Exactly one edited complete screen.
screens.description: Mixed open-contour patch geometry for source and stems, curved waveform end brackets, one chamfered-and-arc-end operator, circular ports and independent curved output cords, inline-underlined numeric controls, circular/diamond toggles, unboxed inspector and underlined navigation.
invariants: unit~ identity and morning-study project retained
24-second source and all four 24-second stems at 44.1 kHz
separate~ directly fans out independently to vocals~, drums~, bass~, other~
import/export, source/stem preview and global transport retained

qa.visual_inspection: Returned generated image inspected directly before copying.
qa.shape_language: Open group boundaries and curved end brackets replace thick closed waveform boxes; central operator has chamfered left and curved right profile; numbers use underlines; toggles use circles/diamonds; navigation uses underlines.
qa.signal_flow: Four independent cords visibly originate at four separate~ output ports and terminate at distinct vocals, drums, bass, other groups; lower-stem cords route independently through central space.
qa.scope: No program code changed; raster interface concept edit only.

screens.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / ui-mockup.
Edit the supplied ORIGINAL 1536 x 1024 unit~ transcription interface. This is a targeted geometry-and-alignment refinement, not a new design. Keep the product identity, panel positions, typography, white background, black/grey monochrome palette, existing short labels and every function. Keep the actual music waveform, monophonic notes, velocity bars and music-grid content. Preserve the same full-screen proportions, flat screenshot viewpoint and pixel dimensions.
IMPORTANT DESIGN CHANGE: the many outlines must stop feeling like rigid rectangles. Use DIFFERENT FUNCTIONAL SHAPES, restrained and native, rather than turning every box into a big rounded card.
1. Outer app shell: retain the basic full-screen footprint but use fine quiet dividers. Header keeps the exact "u~" mark, "unit~", "project: morning-study" at same positions, file/edit/view at top right. The small logo can be a compact soft-corner outline. Top tabs stay "separate", "transcribe", "compose" in the same order and position; REMOVE all individual tab boxes and the solid rectangular black fill. Mark transcribe by one thin black underline. Simple text tabs.
2. Main "transcribe~" parameter module: REMOVE its heavy closed rectangle. Use thin open corner brackets, short partial side-lines and one small title separator, with lots of white breathing room within existing geometry. Module ports become small black CIRCULAR dots rather than black squares. If any cables are shown, use two tiny smooth black curves at outer margins, no right-angle wiring and no cable over text/content.
3. Numeric controls: label "mode" then a compact underlined "melody" with tiny chevron; "threshold" then underlined "0.55"; "min length" then underlined "0.08". Remove enclosing rectangular number fields. "re-analyze" is compact plain text or a small very subtle oval text control, not a rectangle. Preserve original parameters verbatim.
4. Audio waveform: keep "vocals.wav" and "source" labels above it. REMOVE the enclosing closed waveform box. Show a grey/black vocals waveform over pure white with a SHORT FINE baseline, and soft curve-like crop brackets at the two time endpoints. No large rounded background card. Keep gaps in the waveform. Short endpoint crop handles may be narrow vertical curved parentheses. This is still an interactive waveform editor, not decoration.
5. Note editor: Keep "notes" and "64 notes". REMOVE the heavy closed surrounding container. Use thin OPEN CORNER BRACKETS and a single header separator only. Preserve the RECTANGULAR music grid geometry and pitch rail/keyboard: C4, D4, E4, F4, G4. Rectangular grid cells must remain because they encode pitch and time. HOWEVER individual NOTE DURATION BARS get soft rounded ends: short horizontal capsules of varying lengths with thin black outline and pale grey fill. Selected E4 note remains solid BLACK with the exact white label "E4". Do not use color. Thin black vertical velocity stems remain.
6. RIGHT INSPECTOR stays at same right position. Remove its closed big rectangle and replace with a short header separator and a partial vertical rule. Keep label "note". Rows show "pitch E4 - +", "start 03.1 - +", "length 0.25 - +", "velocity 82 - +", "selected: 1"; values have simple underlines, minus/plus inline with no individual square frames. Keep all values as written. The typography remains exactly small monospaced.
7. "compare", "source", "MIDI", "ready", "export.mid" stay at same lower positions. Source uses a thin underline or a compact black small oval to indicate active, MIDI a text tool; export.mid is a small oval outlined tool, not a rectangular box. Footer still shows "play", "stop", "loop", "112 BPM", "4/4", "stereo", "volume", "-6.0 dB" at same locations. Play/stop can be small circles containing triangle/square, loop can be a simple glyph with label, metadata values inline underlines; volume thin line with a circular thumb. No row of identical boxes.
CRITICAL INVARIANT — PRECISE SHARED TIME:
The supplied source already has vertically corresponding time rulers and aligned playheads. Preserve their alignment exactly. The WAVEFORM TIME AREA directly above and NOTE GRID TIME AREA below MUST have exactly the SAME LEFT x origin after reserving the width of the note-editor piano/pitch rail, exactly the SAME RIGHT x endpoint, and exactly the SAME horizontal bar spacing 1–8. Leave an empty narrow rail to the left of the waveform temporal area equal to the note keyboard rail. Bar ticks "1" to "8" in both editors must stack vertically in the same columns. The ruler start and all beat lines correspond perfectly. Keep a SINGLE thin black PLAYHEAD as one visually continuous straight vertical line crossing waveform, note grid and velocity lane at its current position. Its x coordinate may not shift at the separator or rail. Keep the selected E4 note's original time placement and inspector start 03.1. Add no duplicate playhead.
This revision must feel lighter and less boxy while still unmistakably an experimental audio object tool. Pure white/black/neutral grey. Do not introduce a modern rounded-card dashboard, color, shadows, gradients, texture, gloss, 3D, chat, marketing headings or outside background. Preserve existing labels exactly, don't invent or delete functions. One complete readable screenshot only.

validation.identity: unit~, project: morning-study and three navigation functions retained
validation.content: vocals.wav, melody, 0.55, 0.08, 64 notes, E4, 03.1, 0.25, 82 and all comparison/export controls readable
validation.shape: Distinct functional shapes implemented; music grid retained rectangular geometry; no rounded-card wall
validation.timeline: Waveform and MIDI ruler columns visually aligned; same x-coordinate playhead through waveform and note/velocity panes retained

screens.name: unit~
screens.prompt:
Edit the supplied unit~ compose screen. The user likes its monochrome monospace modular language but finds all the rigid rectangular boxes lifeless. Keep the SAME product, project name, three navigation labels, four music-object classes, detailed music content, phrase A/B structure, 8-bar timing, original screen composition, controls and all readable English wording. This is a shape-language refinement, not a different app.

Make the interface more supple and object-specific WITHOUT turning it into a generic rounded-card dashboard.
1. Remove heavy closed rectangular frames around large modules. Separate their areas with small open corner brackets, short side strokes and a thin title rule; airy white space. A few purposeful chamfered or gently curved edges can remain, but not identical closed rectangles everywhere.
2. Notes are duration strokes with a small softly rounded leading end and an accurate straight duration tail. Preserve their correct start/end positions and music grid. The selected note gets a precise slender outline. Avoid fat pills and decorative blobs.
3. Rhythm is a regular row of small circular trigger pads: filled black when active, hollow circles when inactive. The step positions and all sixteen readable step numbers remain.
4. Chords are vertical stacks of short horizontal pitch strokes, collected by a small curved group bracket and clear chord name. This looks different from rhythm trigger circles; preserve Cmaj, Am, Fmaj, G7.
5. Audio is a free-standing black waveform over a thin time baseline, with small curved trim brackets at its start/end or selected range, not imprisoned in a thick rectangular card.
6. The four music-object modules feed phrase~ through small ROUND ports and four smooth slender curved connectors. Each line has real meaning and should not wander through labels or data.
7. Phrase A and B become clear interval ribbons with a subtly shaped/chamfered leading edge and softly ended tail. Their time endpoints, 4 bars each, and positions on the 8-bar ruler remain precise. Distinguish objects by contour and grouping, not by color.
8. Numeric controls are compact editable numbers with short underlines and adjacent plus/minus affordances, rather than box inside box. Navigation is three simple text tabs with a short black underline for compose. Playback buttons are small round transport controls, secondary commands are plain short labels. Keep everything visibly usable.
9. The u~ logo loses its enclosing square; use just the same small u~ glyph with the unit~ name beside it. Right-hand inspector and left library use open title rules rather than full bounding boxes. Give output~ a thin waveform baseline and a narrow fader, not another card.

Typography stays dark crisp monospaced. Background PURE WHITE. Palette strictly BLACK AND WHITE with very light gray grid guides only. No color, no gradient, no shadows, no glass, no 3D, no hand-drawn doodles, no fancy branding, no stock imagery, no chatbot, no giant headings. The outcome should feel like a clear lively instrument/patch workspace using a few deliberate visual primitives, rather than a mechanical grid of rectangles. Preserve every useful function; do not remove the music editor, library, preview or export. Keep 1536x1024 landscape and match the original chrome dimensions.
